title: Renderer-controlled image copy fetches arbitrary URLs in the main process
reasoning: Both IPC handlers accept a renderer-provided image src and pass it to main-process fetch without restricting scheme, origin, host, redirects, size, or content type. Main-process fetch can bypass renderer CORS and network policy assumptions, so a compromised renderer or XSS path can coerce the desktop app into requesting local network or metadata-service URLs and then decoding the response as an image buffer.
recommendation: Constrain copyable image sources before fetch: allow data:image URLs only within a size limit and allow http(s) only for trusted Windie artifact/image origins, with redirect limits, response size limits, and image content-type validation. Consider requiring artifact IDs rather than arbitrary URLs for backend-hosted images.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The feature metadata lists no linked tests, and the included package scripts only show that Jest exists; there is no included test evidence asserting URL policy for these IPC handlers.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add Jest tests for copyImageToClipboard/register handlers that reject file:, localhost/private-network, untrusted http(s), oversized data URLs, non-image content types, and cross-origin redirects while accepting trusted artifact image URLs.
minimumFixScope: ipc_clipboard_image.cjs and ipc_image_context_menu.cjs URL validation plus focused frontend main-process IPC tests.
